On Mon, Oct 29, 2018 at 2:53 PM <victorh...@gmail.com> wrote:
Phil,

Reading some topics of the group, I saw that multipleGroups() applies for different populations and same test. What I'm looking for is to apply the scale I calculated for a test and therefore a population, to another test and another population. I want the parameters that I calculate for another test to be in the same scale as the ones I did before.

I don't think I follow this. You have two tests, presumably with entirely different items (call them test A and test B), and you want to frist calibrate test A and apply these parameters for test B? How do you go about that? Are the items somehow comparable/parallel? Are the tests even the same length? Without some type of shared information there's no honest way to translate the parameter information. You would have to assume you know the population characteristics of test B first before you could do anything in this setup. It sounds as though you are in a vertical scaling situation, which again can be solved using multipleGroup() by including a bunch of structured NA values (assuming there are some shared items).

Can you shine a light on that?
I saw something about constrains, is that it?
